profile.summary: ERNIE-RNA is a pretrained RNA language model that learns from RNA sequence alone but is given a hint about which bases could pair. It is a modified BERT model whose attention is biased by possible base pairs, trained on 20.4 million non-coding RNA sequences. Given RNA sequences up to 1024 nucleotides, it returns sequence and per-base embeddings and attention maps; the repository also ships fine-tuned heads for secondary structure, 3D closeness and 5' UTR mean ribosome load prediction.

summary_quotes.text: ERNIE-RNA distinguishes itself by incorporating a base-pairing-informed attention bias during the calculation of attention scores.
was pre-trained with 20.4 million non-coding RNA sequences from RNAcentral via self-supervised learning
the current model has a sequence length constraint of 1024 nucleotides
This section describes how to use ERNIE-RNA to predict mean ribosome loading (MRL) for 5' UTR RNA sequences

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: ERNIE-RNA follows the BERT design: 12 transformer blocks, each with 12 attention heads over a 768-dimensional token embedding, about 86 million parameters in total. Its change is an all-against-all pairwise bias added to the attention scores, which gives the model prior knowledge of which bases could pair. It was pretrained with masked language modelling: about 15% of nucleotide tokens are replaced and the model predicts them with a cross-entropy loss. The authors report that the attention maps of the pretrained model already capture secondary structure without fine-tuning.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: One pretrained checkpoint is released (ERNIE-RNA_pretrain.pt), together with fine-tuned checkpoints: six for secondary structure prediction, each tied to a training set (bpRNA-1m, RNAStralign, RIVAS, RNA3DB, a frozen bpRNA-1m model used for bpRNA-new, and bpRNA-1m plus RNAStralign), one for 3D closeness and one for UTR mean ribosome load. All are downloaded from a Google Drive folder with no version tags. A result should name the checkpoint file, the dataset_name used for structure prediction, and the repository commit; this page read commit 43bc06de.

We further filtered out sequences longer than 1024 and obtained a large-scale pre-training dataset consisting of 20.4 million ncRNA sequences ultimately.
Analysis of this dataset revealed a substantial proportion of rRNA and tRNA sequences

run_guide.summary: Clone ERNIE-RNA at a pinned commit, build the Linux conda environment, place the pretrained checkpoint, and extract embeddings and attention maps for the bundled test sequences.
prerequisites: conda on Linux. The environment pins python 3.9.16, pytorch 1.10.0 with CUDA 11.3 and fairseq 0.12.2. CPU environments exist for macOS and Windows.
ERNIE-RNA_pretrain.pt, downloaded by hand from the README's Google Drive folder into ./checkpoint/ERNIE-RNA_checkpoint/, the script's default path. No licence is stated for it.
A GPU for the command as written; GPU type and memory are not stated.

limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
The README activates an environment named ERNIE-RNA, but environment.yml names it ERBR-RNA; this guide uses the name from the file.
The README passes --device='cuda:0', which the script's integer argument would reject; this guide uses --device 0.
The checkpoint download from Google Drive is manual; the sources give no command for it.
